solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something immune to challenge, customs-wise, landed aboard boat

indicators.note: one thing goes on board, that is inside, the boat

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
acred = owning land, as in the landed gentry

explanation.surface: Someone who owns land and lives on a boat seems to be beyond the reach of customs officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs-wise' belongs to the definition: a sacred cow is untouchable by custom, not by the customs service. ACRED is an old word for owning acres.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is a custom or institution that nobody is allowed to question.

clue.text: Caught half-a-dozen cats

indicators.note: caught by the ear, that is heard

explanation.surface: Someone has trapped six cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like a noun but is a verb: to cat is slang for to vomit, so it cats = it sicks.
explanation.definitionFit: To cat is British slang for to be sick, so cats means sicks.

clue.text: Wake up, time for school — change, not having cold to get over

parts.note: SWITCH without C (cold, as on a tap)

explanation.surface: A child is told to get up because school has started again, and must adjust to the change without having a cold as an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes of the surface hide a plain charade: three pieces laid end to end, the last with one letter missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain idiom: getting over a loss and accepting it are the same act.

clue.text: Might I pass exam, scoring 50 per cent? See you at half-term

indicators.note: only half the word is used

parts.note: CU is text-speak for see you
the first half of SEMESTER, a term

explanation.surface: A pupil worries about scraping through an exam and says goodbye until the half-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-term' reads as the school holiday but splits into its parts: half of a word meaning term. A semester is an academic term, mostly in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: "Excuse me" is what you say when asking to squeeze past someone.

clue.text: State where Congress banned a bicycle, bizarrely

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: The US Congress has passed a strange law banning bicycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' and 'Congress' pull toward American politics; here congress means sexual intercourse, and the state is a condition, not Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibacy is the condition of abstaining from sex, or congress.

clue.text: Rugby score underpinning victory characteristic of season

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that underpins sits below the other

parts.note: a try is the main score in rugby

explanation.surface: A late try in rugby clinches a win typical of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: wintry is characteristic of one season in particular, and the surface's sporting season is a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry describes things characteristic of winter, a season.

clue.text: Person with plenty of time dismantled rifle

indicators.note: taken apart and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with time on their hands strips down a rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plenty of time' sounds like leisure; it is a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, a person with plenty of time to do.

clue.text: US cops on leave picked up devoted admirer

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the LAPD is the Los Angeles Police Department

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

explanation.surface: American police officers on leave are seen as somebody's adoring fans.
explanation.walkthrough: GO read upwards gives OG under LAPD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a fawning follower, someone slavishly devoted to another person.

clue.text: Force freedom in hearing where criminals once hung mischief-maker

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

indicators.note: the word is taken as it is heard, not spelt

explanation.surface: A court hearing is forced on a trickster, with talk of freedom and of the old gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle piece is a sound; F and GIBBET are spelt as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a flighty, frivolous person; the name was once also given to an imp or mischief-maker.

clue.text: Tie once more, going round course at which most won't reach finish line?

definitions.text: at which most won't reach finish line?
definitions.note: the definition is a description, standing for 'a race at which…'

parts.note: AYR, a Scottish racecourse, with its A cycled to the end

explanation.surface: Someone reties a shoelace on a course where most competitors never get to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In a relay only the last runner of each team crosses the line, which is why most won't reach it. AYR is a racecourse town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay race only the anchor runners finish, so most runners never reach the line.

clue.text: Funny mineral found in mountain pass

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other

parts.note: a col is a pass between peaks

explanation.surface: An odd mineral has turned up in a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' in the surface means strange; as the definition it means amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something comical makes you laugh, which is what funny means here.

clue.text: Unplait curls for wedding

indicators.note: the letters twist round into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride undoes her plaits and curls her hair for the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curls' reads as hair styling; it is telling the letters of UNPLAIT to twist into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to a wedding, as in nuptial vows.

clue.text: Positions spectacles on one's ears?

indicators.note: the word as it falls on the ears, heard not seen

explanation.surface: Someone perches a pair of glasses on their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacles sit on the ears in the surface; here they are sights, and the ears are listening.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a site is the place where something is put, its position.

clue.text: Altercation between boozer and son, a wheeler-dealer?

indicators.note: the quarrel word is placed between the pub word and the son word

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, which has a bar
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out between a man in the pub and his son, a shady trader perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrow boy is a London street trader selling from a handcart; the question mark marks the pun on 'wheeler', since his barrow has wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A street trader pushing a wheeled cart is a small-time dealer, literally one who deals from wheels.

clue.text: Mother stopping in city destroyed close relationship

indicators.note: the mother word stops up a gap, sitting inside the scrambled letters
the city is destroyed, so the letters of 'in city' are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother stays on in a ruined city, in a scene of wartime devastation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges IN CITY into INTICY; MA goes inside to give INTI-MA-CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimacy is closeness or familiarity between people, a close personal bond.

clue.text: It could be theft of internal post

definitions.meaning: a crime carried out by someone on the staff
a post is a job, and internal means inside

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether things vanishing from the internal mail are being stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a crime committed by someone on the staff; the second is simply a job, or post, inside the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a theft by someone within the organisation, and it is also literally a post inside it.

clue.text: Solo number from West Side Story missing intro

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: "Maria" is a song from the musical West Side Story

explanation.surface: A solo song from West Side Story is performed without its introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo number' is the definition, not the song being described; the song is Maria.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo piece for voice, in opera especially.

clue.text: Monkey to stroll scratching tail in souk?

indicators.note: in places the shortened stroll inside the market

parts.note: a souk is an Arab market, a mart

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, here the final letter

parts.note: to mosey is to stroll along slowly

explanation.surface: A monkey wanders through a souk scratching its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: A souk is a market in an Arab city; mosey is an informal American word for wandering along, and 'tail' is its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey with a long tail.

clue.text: Vintage candle, perhaps one separated from candle-holder?

parts.note: a candle gives a flame; 'perhaps' flags the loose link

explanation.surface: An antique candle, perhaps one parted from its candlestick.
explanation.walkthrough: The candle-holder is not a candlestick but someone who still holds a candle for a former lover, and the old flame is that lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former lover; to hold a candle for someone is to still carry a torch for them.

clue.text: Angry god from the east

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: Eros, the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A god arrives from the east in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Sore for angry is chiefly American usage, as in a sore loser.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use, chiefly American: to be sore at someone is to be cross with them.

clue.text: Fix data set for digital manager

parts.note: a computer file is a set of data

explanation.surface: Correcting a dataset for someone who manages digital systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means relating to digits, that is fingers; the manager is what keeps fingernails in trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file manages the nails on your digits, your fingers.

clue.text: Trade union beset by enemies, one needing Labour in due course

definitions.text: one needing Labour in due course

indicators.note: surrounded on all sides by the enemies

explanation.surface: A trade union, surrounded by enemies, needs the Labour Party to come good eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the British political party; here it is childbirth, which the foetus will need at the due date.
explanation.definitionFit: A foetus awaits labour, the process of birth, when it is due.

clue.text: Crown land regularly seized by parliament, but not last month

indicators.note: the picked letters are taken inside the shortened assembly word
the assembly word loses its final letter

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan or historic Germany

indicators.note: every other letter of land is used, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A crown seizes land with the help of parliament, a constitutional row from the history books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parliament' looks like Westminster, but a diet is the name for some national assemblies, such as Japan's.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled headband worn as a symbol of royalty, a kind of crown.

clue.text: Dictatorship decides pot is malevolent to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of 'decides' to the first letter of 'malevolent'

explanation.surface: A dictator decides that a drug is harmful, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words, starting inside 'decides' and ending on the first letter of 'malevolent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rule by a single absolute tyrant.

clue.text: Trifle endlessly, frolicking

indicators.note: frolicking suggests playful movement, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone playing about with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIFL (trifle without its end) is rearranged; the whole clue also describes what a flirt does.
explanation.definitionFit: To flirt is to play at love, dallying lightheartedly without serious intent.

clue.text: Reject scripture being brought up — it's poisonous

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun: something poisonous

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing up means lifting the letters so they read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a piece of scripture that is being quoted, calling it poison.
explanation.walkthrough: NIX and OT are joined and then the whole reversed, so OT ends up first.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause standing for the noun: a toxin is a poison made by a living organism.

clue.text: Articulate sign up for series of talks

parts.note: to sign up for a club or cause is to join it
TED is the well-known series of short recorded lectures, the TED Talks

explanation.surface: Someone eloquent enrolling to give one of those inspirational lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective meaning eloquent, but here it is the zoologist's sense of having joints, as in an articulated limb or lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulate structure is one made of segments connected by hinges, which is exactly what a jointed one is.

clue.text: Drama (TV) where politicians took a stand

parts.note: the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A TV drama about where politicians made their stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took a stand' reads as adopting a position; literally, speakers once stood on a crate to address crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: A soapbox is the crate a public speaker stands on to harangue a crowd.

clue.text: Stretch of forest habitat around bits of Thailand

indicators.note: a stretch is only part of the text
the letters are read the other way round

explanation.surface: A stretch of forest habitat around parts of Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'forest habitat' to find the answer. The baht is Thailand's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahts are units of Thai currency, so bits of Thailand's money.

clue.text: Shabby, dilapidated home: a tent

indicators.note: falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's shabby, run-down home turns out to be a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dilapidated' fits the surface as a description of the tent but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative use: clothes chewed by moths look worn, so anything tatty is so described.
